subject: URG: DPA notification & communications — proposed timelines and evidence path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA notification & communications — proposed timelines and evidence path

Tom — thanks again for the conversation this morning. To make progress on the remaining DPA points from your legal/security teams, I've sketched a short notification and cooperation protocol that we can convert into a narrow amendment rather than reworking the full DPA. High level proposal: 

- Notification windows: initial acknowledgement to customer security contact within 4 hours of detection, substantive notification within 48 hours for incidents that materially affect Greenline users (we propose thresholds below).
- Scope: incidents that result in confirmed unauthorized access or exfiltration of customer data, or any event required to be reported under jurisdictional law.
- Evidence & cooperation: Redwood will provide an initial incident summary and hashes/artifacts within 48 hours where feasible, followed by a forensic report within 30 days. We will share subprocessor evidence where applicable.
- Thresholds: we recommend the principle-based approach (sensitivity + scope) rather than a strict customer-count trigger. Example: any exposure of PHI or regulated PII triggers the 48-hour substantive notification regardless of count; for non-sensitive PII, use a 5,000-account threshold.

I've attached a short evidence-request checklist to show the artifacts we can provide quickly. If that approach sounds reasonable, Rishi and Laura from Legal/Security will draft suggested contract language and we can route a short amendment through DocuSign.

Next steps: Tom / Greenline security — confirm whether the 4-hour ack + 48-hour substantive window is acceptable and whether the threshold examples make sense. If you prefer different timing for regulated data, call that out and we will adjust.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0187

Attachment: GLH-evidence-request-checklist.pdf (summary list of artifacts: timeline exports, syslogs, SSO assertion logs, sample redacted records)

Vanessa — appreciate the clear proposal. A few quick clarifying points from our side: 

1) For regulated PHI, our compliance team would prefer a 24-hour substantive notification window (not 48). Is Redwood able to commit to an accelerated path when the data involved meets HIPAA definitions?
2) We need an explicit lane for preserved forensic evidence. Will Redwood agree to preserve imaging / full forensic captures for 90 days on request?
3) Subprocessor transparency: can you confirm the current subprocessor registry and whether Redwood will provide timely notice when a subprocessor change affects Greenline's processing?

I'll loop in our external counsel (Ava Collins) for anything contract-y, and our security inbox for technical coordination.

Regards,
Tom Harris

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA notification & communications — proposed timelines and evidence path

Tom / Vanessa — please find below proposed contract wording that we think balances the operational needs you described with Redwood's constraints. This is intentionally concise and limited to an amendment.

1) Incident notification
"Redwood will acknowledge receipt of an incident report from Customer within four (4) hours of detection or, if earlier, within four (4) hours of Redwood becoming aware of the Event. For Events involving Customer Data constituting Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under applicable law, Redwood will provide a substantive notification to Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of detection. For Events involving regulated personal data or Customer-sensitive PII that materially affect Customer accounts, Redwood will provide a substantive notification within forty-eight (48) hours. For other confirmed unauthorized access resulting in exfiltration of non-sensitive personal data, Redwood will provide a substantive notification within seventy-two (72) hours.

2) Evidence preservation and transfer
"Upon Customer request, Redwood will preserve forensic images, logs, and related artifacts for a period of ninety (90) days and will, subject to reasonable security and operational constraints, provide copies or secure access to such artifacts to Customer or Customer's retained forensic vendor. Transfer will be accomplished via mutually agreed secure transfer (e.g., encrypted archive or temporary secure repository). Redwood will redact logs to remove unrelated customer data prior to transfer where technically necessary, and will document redaction steps.

3) Subprocessors and notice
"Redwood maintains an up-to-date subprocessor registry and will provide Customer with thirty (30) days' advance notice of material additions or changes. For changes that are deployed urgently or in response to a security issue, Redwood will provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable and offer mitigation alternatives.

Comments: - We intentionally preserved a tiered timing approach rather than a single numeric-only threshold. That should address PHI concerns and leave room for operational judgment where counts are noisy.

If this looks good to Greenline, Laura and I can fold it into the draft amendment and we can route to DocuSign.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
